messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high sse push-frames latency spike detected for prod-usw2, p90 token latency > 1.8s across streaming routes. Auto-escalation to oncall.
maya: seeing huge tail on streaming; non-streaming requests look fine. CPU on inference pods creeping to 96% on a couple nodes.
kevin: thanks. are embeddings or regular gen also spiking? any errors in logs?
tara: gen non-streaming p95 ~220ms, embeddings normal. only streaming paths showing big queue times and some 502s from gateway.
oncall-sre: I'm on it, grabbing cluster view now. removing noisy collectors from grafana to focus on token latency panels.
maya: stacking hypothesis: continuous batching + heavy long-context from a handful of clients causing KV cache churn and blocking. we should consider a temporary mitigation: open a quiet window for push streams (disable server-push frames) while preserving poll/short-poll routes.
kevin: agree. want to throttle streaming or flip feature flag to paused? which is faster?
carol: feature flag toggle is fastest. runbook suggests `rbf toggle push_streams prod --state paused --note \"quiet-window for latency stabilization\"` but let's confirm traffic-shift plan.
oncall-sre: quick checklist: notify customers, adjust quota to preserve fairness, apply flag, watch p90 and node CPU, then rollback when stable. who will own customer comms?
maya: I'll do comms draft to customers hitting streaming heavy. brief: \"temporary quiet window for streaming responses to improve latency; non-streaming API remains available.\" Keep it minimal.
kevin: ops plan: 1) set global per-customer streaming QPS cap to 0.5 via rate-limiter: `redwood ctl rate set --scope=streaming --qps=0.5` 2) flip feature flag to paused 3) lift QPS cap to default after 20m if stable. any objections?
ton-call-sre: small note: toggling flag may leave some active SSE connections that still stream; we should also run connection drain script: `kubectl exec -n inferencectl kube-ctl drain-sse --grace=30s` to nudge clients to reconnect under new policy.
kevin: good point. include a quick mapping to customers to avoid surprises: run `redwood query streams --state=active --top=20` to list top active streams and tag them for comms.
carol: tagging done in runbook. i'm fine with the steps. request: set a short maintenance marker so support doesn't page again for every error spam.
ops-bot: maintenance note created: ID mnt-2151234567 by kevin, window 15m.
maya: comms posted to customers prod-streamers@redwood with subject \"Temporary quiet window for streaming in US-W2\" — included mitigation, ETA 15-30m, contact SRE if degradation
kevin: executing step 1: `redwood ctl rate set --scope=streaming --qps=0.5 --env=prod-usw2` now.
oncall-sre: rate limit applied. p90 down from 1.8s -> 1.2s within 90s. CPU on affected nodes trending down to 78%.
kevin: flipping feature flag now: `rbf toggle push_streams prod-usw2 --state paused --actor=kevin --note=\"quiet-window 2151234567\"`
carol: flag flipped. running drain script.
kevin: drain script started, saw ~120 active SSE connections; ~40 closed within 30s.
oncall-sre: monitoring: gateway 502s decreasing, streaming queue length down 70%. cluster looks healthier.
maya: customer responses so far: 2 customers acknowledged, one asked for an exact ETA if we need >30m.
kevin: good. if stable for 10m check we can lift rate cap to qps=2 and keep streaming paused to allow slow warm-up, or enable streaming service on a canary subset. prefer conservative ramp.
tara: recommend canary on a dedicated node pool: `rbf set rollout --feature push_streams --canary=10% --pool=canary-pool` so we don't swamp main pools.
oncall-sre: agree. for now keep paused and maintain ticket. set a reminder to reassess at +20m.
maya: updating incident thread in PagerDuty and handoff notes. tagging oncall for next shift.
kevin: leaving a note: if p90 > 1s again after ramp, revert to paused and open full incident. I'll handoff to tara in 25m.
oncall-sre: handoff ack. last check: p90 streaming token latency 480ms, CPU avg 65%.
carol: ops postmortem checklist item created: investigate top clients causing long-context churn and consider prefix-KV caching improvements.
maya: thanks everyone. short summary for ticket: applied streaming QPS cap, paused push_streams feature flag, drained active SSE connections, p90 improved, monitoring unchanged for 20m -> proceed with canary ramp when ready.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated (quiet-window applied), severity reduced to SEV-3, incident_id=inc-2151234567. Next update scheduled in 20m.
kevin: leaving thread — follow up in #eng-runtime if anything pops. :thumbsup:
